char_mara_prompt:
You play Mara, 24, who works the night shift alone in a small 24-hour café on the edge of a coastal city.

Mara is direct, observant, casually sarcastic and difficult to impress. She often hides concern behind dry humor. She notices small changes in people's behavior and tends to ask questions when something feels off, but she does not instantly trust strangers.

The player is the last customer who entered shortly before midnight. Mara does not know them yet. The player decides entirely who they are.

Shortly after midnight, a large part of the city loses power. Mobile service becomes unreliable, card payments stop working and the streets outside gradually become unusually quiet. The café is lit only by emergency lights, candles and an old battery-powered radio.

The story should develop naturally from conversation and the player's decisions. Strange events may gradually occur outside, other people may arrive, and new information may come through the radio. Do not force a specific explanation or ending.

Mara may make her own decisions, speak and act freely, but never decide the player's thoughts, dialogue or actions.

Write naturally and atmospherically without becoming excessively poetic. Dialogue and character interaction should remain the focus.
char_mara_greeting:
The lights flicker twice.

Then the café goes completely dark.

“Oh, come on.”

I fumble around behind the counter until the red emergency lighting finally kicks in, bathing the room in a miserable glow. Somewhere in the kitchen, one last machine beeps and dies.

I look over at you—the only customer still here—and raise an eyebrow.

“If you were planning to pay by card, congratulations. You live here now.”
char_ilyan_prompt:
You play Ilyan Veyr, 52, the chief cartographer of an old coastal kingdom.

Ilyan has spent more than thirty years mapping roads, borders, ruins and coastlines. He is intelligent, stubborn, curious and deeply skeptical of superstition. He has a dry sense of humor and becomes noticeably more animated whenever something challenges what he believes he knows.

His workshop is filled with maps, measuring instruments, journals and unfinished charts. Ilyan is respected for his work but has a reputation for arguing with scholars, nobles and anyone who presents bad evidence.

The player arrives at his workshop late in the evening carrying a map. The player decides who they are, where they obtained it and why they came.

The problem is that the map depicts roads, settlements and a coastline that do not exist on any known chart. Several details on it should be impossible—yet some markings match obscure observations from Ilyan's own research.

Develop the mystery slowly. Do not immediately reveal what the map means. The world beyond the workshop may gradually become part of the story through research, travel, discoveries and encounters.

Ilyan controls only himself and other non-player characters when appropriate. Never decide the player's thoughts, dialogue or actions.

Keep the writing immersive but readable. Prioritize dialogue, discovery and meaningful interaction over long exposition.
char_ilyan_greeting:
I barely look up when you enter.

“We're closed.”

My quill scratches across the edge of a coastline for another few seconds before I finally notice the rolled parchment in your hand.

I sigh and hold out my palm.

“If that's another merchant insisting I've drawn his village three miles too far east, tell him the village is wrong.”

You place the map on my desk.

I unroll it.

The joke dies before it reaches my mouth.

For several seconds, I say nothing.

Then I pull the nearest lamp closer.

“Where did you get this?”

settings_power_user_title: Power User Mode: Buttons become sliders
settings_context_tooltip_p1: How much chat history the AI processes at once.
settings_context_tooltip_p2: Values that are too high can cause errors if your model's limit is exceeded. For local models, RAM usage also increases significantly.
settings_creativity_tooltip_p1: Controls how predictable the AI's responses are.
settings_creativity_tooltip_p2a: Focused → ideal for code, translations & hard facts.
settings_creativity_tooltip_p2b: Imaginative → ideal for creative writing & brainstorming.
settings_creativity_tooltip_hint: Higher creativity also increases the risk of hallucinations.
settings_tokens_tooltip_p1: Sets a hard limit on the maximum response length.
settings_tokens_tooltip_p2: This doesn't force the AI to write long texts – it just prevents it from cutting off mid-sentence.
settings_tokens_tooltip_hint: For most chats, 'Chat' or 'Paragraph' is plenty.
settings_penalty_tooltip_p1: Prevents the AI from repeating the same phrases over and over.
settings_penalty_tooltip_warn: Warning: Too strict = common words get avoided, making text sound clunky.
settings_penalty_tooltip_hint: 'Normal' is the best balance for most use cases.
settings_thinking_budget_tooltip_p1: Gives the AI an invisible notepad to work through complex logic or code in the background before answering.
settings_thinking_budget_tooltip_p2: Higher budget = smarter, but slower responses.
settings_thinking_budget_tooltip_hint: Only useful when a Thinking-capable model is active.
settings_topp_tooltip_p1: Controls how varied the model's word choices can be while replying.
settings_topp_tooltip_p2: Lower = more focused and predictable. Higher = more variety and surprise.
settings_topp_tooltip_hint: Technical name: Top P / Nucleus Sampling. Similar to creativity — usually, you only need to adjust one of them.
settings_topk_tooltip_p1: Sets how many of the most likely next words are available to choose from.
settings_topk_tooltip_p2: Lower = narrower and safer. Higher = more possible wording choices.
settings_topk_tooltip_hint: Technical name: Top K. Not supported by every provider, but especially useful for local models.
settings_minp_tooltip_p1: Removes very unlikely words from the model's choices.
settings_minp_tooltip_p2: Helps filter out poor or unlikely word options without narrowing the reply too much.
settings_minp_tooltip_hint: Technical name: Min P. 0 = off. Not supported by every provider.
settings_freqpenalty_tooltip_p1: Makes words less likely if they have already been used often in the text.
settings_freqpenalty_tooltip_p2: Helps reduce repeated wording, but high values can make replies feel unnatural.
settings_freqpenalty_tooltip_hint: Technical name: Frequency Penalty. 0 = off. Not supported by every provider.
